qs.q: A patient presents with malar rash, discoid rash, arthritis, and a positive antinuclear antibody test, but lacks immunological criteria beyond the ANA. According to the classification rules, why might this patient not be fully categorized under certain strict multi-criteria groups?
o: Classification of malar and discoid rashes as mutually exclusive findings
Lack of at least one specific immunologic criterion beyond basic ANA
Failure of a positive ANA to count toward the total diagnostic criteria
Exclusion of arthritis as a valid clinical criterion in modern scoring systems
qs.e: Certain classification schemes mandate specific combinations, such as having at least one clinical and one immunologic criterion, meaning general criteria alone without required immunologic subgroups may fail classification.

qs.q: A 30-year-old woman being evaluated for joint pain is found to have a positive antinuclear antibody titer of 1:640. Which statement best describes the clinical utility of this test in systemic lupus erythematosus?
o: It is found in over 98% of patients but lacks diagnostic specificity.
It directly correlates with the current disease activity score.
It rules out other overlapping connective tissue disorders.
It confirms the diagnosis of lupus when present in healthy adults.
qs.e: A positive ANA is present in over 98% of SLE patients, but because it can also be found in healthy individuals and other conditions, it is not diagnostic on its own. It also does not correlate well with disease activity for most patients.
